clue.text: Ghostly appearance of horse without carriage

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the horse word goes round the carriage word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a horse-drawn carriage for hire

explanation.surface: A spectral sight: a horse seen running with no carriage behind it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'appearance of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something macabre is gruesome and deathly, close in feel to the eerie and spectral.

clue.text: Surgical cover many enquire after

indicators.note: after places the enquiring word behind the word for many

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many
to ask is to enquire

explanation.surface: Many people ask questions about the face covering a surgeon wears.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wear a mask over nose and mouth as a protective covering in theatre.

clue.text: Bill turned in a murderer

indicators.note: turned means the word for bill is read backwards

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill handed in a killer to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Cain killed his brother Abel, the first murderer in the Bible.

clue.text: Divisions used in local government or in branches

indicators.note: the second in puts the little word inside the word for branches

parts.note: boughs are the branches of a tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: Administrative units in local government or in some branch offices.
explanation.definitionFit: Boroughs are administrative districts with their own councils, units of local government.

clue.text: Nun that is adjusting to the tedium of life

indicators.note: adjusting means rearranging these letters into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A nun coming to terms with the dullness of convent routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness and boredom with daily existence.

clue.text: He's in the firing line

parts.note: firing here means feeding a furnace or boiler, not shooting; this man shovels coal into it

explanation.surface: A man under attack, standing where the shots fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker tends the fire of a steam engine or ship's boiler, so works on the firing line.

clue.text: Hammer thrower has a number on his chest

parts.note: Thor, the Norse god, hurled his hammer Mjolnir
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: An athlete in the hammer event wears a competitor number on his chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer thrower' suggests an athlete; it is the Norse god.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorax is the anatomical name for the chest cavity and the part of the body around it.

clue.text: They're only one step up from the gutter

definitions.text: They're only one step up from the gutter

parts.words: They're only one step up from the gutter
parts.note: reads as down-and-outs barely above destitution, but literally means the raised stones edging a pavement

explanation.surface: People who have barely escaped total poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones form the raised edge of the pavement, a step up from the roadside channel.

clue.text: Reserves have to practise during breaks

indicators.note: during puts the practising inside the breaks

parts.note: rests are breaks from activity
to train is to practise

explanation.surface: Reserve players must keep training even in their rest periods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserves' looks like substitute players; it is the noun for curbs or self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in the sense of self-control and holding back corresponds to restraint.

clue.text: Prison clique causing trouble

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
a ring is a closed group or clique

explanation.surface: A gang inside a jail stirring up unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirring up means provoking agitation, so stirring is making mischief.

clue.text: Stage directors make them up

definitions.meaning: a name for the theatre stage
company directors together form a governing body

explanation.surface: Theatre directors build their own sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards are both the stage of a theatre and the governing bodies made up of company directors.

clue.text: There's confusion in the Old Testament

indicators.note: confusion means the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Muddled passages are found in the Hebrew scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles THERES (the S of the contraction counts).
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is one of the books found in the Old Testament, named after its Jewish queen.

clue.text: He received his final rents mid-month

definitions.text: He received his final rents mid-month

parts.words: He received his final rents mid-month
parts.note: reads like a landlord collecting money, but rents are tears or stab wounds received on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: A landlord collected his last payments halfway through the month.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ides of March, the 15th, was when Brutus and the conspirators stabbed the dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dictator was assassinated with many stab wounds on the Ides of March, mid-month.

clue.text: Currently come and go

parts.note: currently plays on a current of water: the tide recedes and returns

explanation.surface: Things that are fleeting these days.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide's going out and coming in is described as this phrase, also used for any rise and fall.

clue.text: Female supporter at the match

parts.note: suggests a woman fan at a football game, but the match is a wedding

explanation.surface: A woman cheering on a team at a football game.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends and supports the bride at her wedding, a match in the marital sense.

clue.text: Delivery is not left, though one is entitled to it

parts.note: delivery of a baby is its birth
the side that is not left is right

explanation.surface: A parcel that is correctly delivered, which the addressee has every right to.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthright is something a person has a claim to from the day they were born.

clue.text: A section of the foot soldiers should be

definitions.meaning: the arched middle part of the foot
marching soldiers should keep together, all feet moving at once

explanation.surface: Infantry must be in a particular part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The instep is the upper middle of the foot; marching soldiers should be in step.

clue.text: Sash 50% too big

indicators.note: 50% asks for a run half as long as the six letters of the phrase, taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A sash fifty per cent too large.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of three is taken from the middle of TOOBIG.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash tied around a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Agreement among different unions

parts.note: among means in

indicators.note: different means the letters take another arrangement

explanation.surface: Several trade unions finding common ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in unison means acting together in full accord.

clue.text: Help one gets in this day and age

indicators.note: gets in puts the numeral inside the era abbreviation

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the current era
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Help is something a person receives in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid is assistance or support, the same as help.

clue.text: Following terrible strain chap becomes acerbic

indicators.note: following puts the man after the reshuffled letters
terrible means the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: After a dreadful ordeal a man turns bitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and severe, much like acerbic ones.

clue.text: Pass by troubled region

indicators.note: troubled means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Driving past a strife-torn area without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass something by is to disregard or overlook it.

clue.text: Many meetings are disrupted by strife

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, hence many

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: Lots of gatherings are broken up by conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges MEETINGSARE to ISAGREEMENT, after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Disagreement is conflict and dissent, a milder form of open discord.

clue.text: Moira goes out with New Zealander

indicators.note: goes out, as in goes astray, means the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Moira is dating a man from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Indication that there's good starting in evil

indicators.note: starting in means the good letter goes inside the word for evil

parts.note: sin is wrongdoing or evil

explanation.surface: Evidence that virtue may be found where wickedness is.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a mark or token that indicates something.

clue.text: Seek fresh increases

indicators.note: fresh means the letters are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: Searching for further pay rises.
explanation.definitionFit: To eke means, in an old sense, to add to or lengthen something.

clue.text: Persuade one to believe the dog's ready for walkies

definitions.meaning: to deceive someone into thinking something false
a dog's strap has been clipped on so it can be taken out

explanation.surface: Convincing a pet that it is about to go out for a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive them; a dog on its lead is ready to be walked.

clue.text: Girl's given credit as an air-traffic controller

parts.note: Joy is a girl's name, here with its possessive S
tick is slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A woman is praised for her work in an airport control tower.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's control stick steers the aircraft, so it controls traffic in the air in a playful sense.

clue.text: They hold back movement on the western borders

parts.note: edges are borders

explanation.surface: Frontier defences in the west that stop people crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedges are chocks jammed under doors or wheels to stop them moving.

clue.text: Period of play

parts.note: a spell at the crease batting in cricket, or a turn in general

explanation.surface: A stretch of time in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a summer bat-and-ball sport, a side's turn at batting carries this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket and baseball this is the turn of a team or player to bat.
